findings.subject: phase-idg-13
findings.title: phase-idg-13's backfill writes agent-authored terminal-state closes for the whole corpus without depending on phase-idg-14, the phase that builds the required propose/verify/ratify mechanism and proposed_by provenance field.
findings.evidence: GOV-003 (2026-09-22 entry, ~line 622): 'the owner accepted the agent-writable terminal transition, with one condition: an agent-written terminal state announces itself as awaiting review... phase-idg-01 builds it that way or not at all.' GOV-003 (2026-09-23 entry, ~line 696): the authority process (propose/verify/ratify, proposed_by field) split out of phase-idg-01 into phase-idg-14. phase-idg-13's backlog.yaml entry has `depends_on: [phase-idg-01]` only -- no phase-idg-14 -- and its scope has an agent sweep the whole idea log and 'close each into the state its own finding evidences,' with acceptance criteria ('Every idea closed by this phase carries a pointer that resolves', 'The seven ideas named in scope are closed...') that never mention proposed_by or a ratification step.
findings.consequence: If phase-idg-13 runs once phase-idg-01 ships (its only declared dependency), it will write terminal-state closes for potentially the full corpus as unilateral agent writes -- exactly the 'or not at all' case the owner ruled out. Because the idea log is append-only, fixing this after the fact means appending correction events over every close the backfill wrote, not editing them.
findings.minimal_fix: Add phase-idg-14 to phase-idg-13's depends_on, and add an acceptance line requiring each backfilled close to carry proposed_by and be marked pending ratification.

findings.subject: phase-idg-14
findings.title: The GOV-003 coordination note pairing the idea-log terminal-state mechanism with phase-irs-09's separate 'delivered' path is attached only to phase-idg-01's next_action, not to phase-idg-14, which is now the phase that actually builds that mechanism.
findings.evidence: GOV-003 (~line 597-600): 'One delivered, two paths into it... The pipeline implements a second path into it rather than inventing a parallel one. Whoever builds either phase reads the other first.' phase-idg-01's next_action in backlog.yaml quotes this note; phase-idg-14's next_action (added 2026-09-23, batch-003 Q4) only points at the batch-003 entry (~line 696-725) and never mentions phase-irs-09 or the 'two paths into delivered' reasoning anywhere in its scope, acceptance or next_action.
findings.consequence: An agent building phase-idg-14 following only its own next_action will not be pointed at phase-irs-09's parallel Gate-5 sign-off path into `delivered`, risking two inconsistent mechanisms (one with proposed_by provenance, one without) writing the same terminal status.
findings.minimal_fix: Copy the 'reads the other first' cross-reference to phase-irs-09 into phase-idg-14's next_action, since phase-idg-14 -- not phase-idg-01 -- now owns the mechanism the note is about.

findings.subject: phase-idg-14
findings.title: phase-idg-14's deliverables omit .claude/agents/, even though its scope requires building two new agents (a proposer and a verifier) that do not exist in the repository today.
findings.evidence: phase-idg-14 scope: 'Build the two-agent authority process for reaching a terminal state... an agent proposes the close with its evidence... a second agent verifies the pointer resolves.' Its deliverables list is `schemas/idea.schema.json`, `tools/append_idea.py`, `src/db/ideas.py`, `test/` -- no `.claude/agents/`. `grep -l -i 'propose\|verify\|ratify\|terminal' .claude/agents/*.md` finds no existing agent implementing this (the only idea-related agent, idea-triage.md, explicitly states 'Never advances an idea past triaged, never merges or declines one'). By contrast, phase-irs-09, a comparably-scoped 'build the realization agent' phase, does list `.claude/agents/` in its deliverables.
findings.consequence: The phase's most concrete build artifact is undeclared, so the governance conflicts check cannot flag a collision if another concurrent phase also touches `.claude/agents/`, and a builder scoping the phase from `deliverables` alone would miss that new agent definition files are required.

findings.subject: phase-idg-01
findings.title: Declared systems omit sys-governance despite a deliverable (src/governance/) that only that system covers, and correcting it breaks the plan's own claimed disjoint-parallel-front.
findings.evidence: backlog.yaml lines 9814-9816: phase-idg-01 declares systems: [sys-contracts, sys-portfolio]. Its deliverables (line 9856) include src/governance/, which docs/08-governance/systems.yaml lines 343-350 assigns to sys-governance, not sys-contracts or sys-portfolio (that deliverable was added by the 2026-09-23 batch-003 Q8 fix per GOV-003 line 715). Meanwhile phase-idg-06 (backlog.yaml line 10111-10112) already declares systems: [sys-governance]. PLAN-029 lines 192-202 names phase-idg-01 + phase-idg-06 + phase-idg-10 as 'the one mutually disjoint set' and 'the widest genuinely parallel front... reached at the start' — a claim GOV-010 P7 cites by name as this plan's exemplar of correct collision accounting.
findings.consequence: As declared today, a real collision on the governance-check internals between phase-idg-01 and phase-idg-06 is invisible to src/governance/backlog.py's collision detector (concurrency_errors only compares declared systems and deliverable paths). Declaring it correctly, the minimal fix, makes phase-idg-01 and phase-idg-06 collide on sys-governance and falsifies the plan's own stated disjoint trio and its execution-order recommendation.
findings.minimal_fix: Add sys-governance to phase-idg-01's systems, and correct PLAN-029's execution-order section to state that phase-idg-01 and phase-idg-06 in fact collide.

findings.subject: phase-idg-01
findings.title: No document names the schema transition edge phase-idg-13 needs (discarded -> resolved), and it conflicts with the schema's own stated design.
findings.evidence: schemas/idea.schema.json line 292's description: 'discarded is reachable from every working state but is never a from — the one way out of it is a revisited event' (which returns the idea to reviewing, per line ~456's description, not to any terminal state directly). phase-idg-13's scope (backlog.yaml line 9894) literally requires: 'Move 000099 and 000129 from discarded to resolved.' A direct fold-in of status(from: discarded, to: resolved) would violate the stated design; going through revisited lands the idea in reviewing first. Confirmed via _data/ideas.jsonl: both 000099 and 000129 currently sit at a single triaged->discarded status event with zero prior revisited events, so no existing mechanism gets them to resolved. Neither phase-idg-01's scope (which builds the schema) nor GOV-003's entry (lines 607-612) states which mechanism is intended.
findings.consequence: Built literally as scoped, phase-idg-01 may not produce a schema phase-idg-13 can satisfy without someone deciding, unrecorded, whether discarded becomes a sanctioned from-state for the new terminal statuses (breaking the documented invariant) or whether the reversal goes through revisited (leaving a reviewing hop the scope text never mentions).
findings.minimal_fix: Add one line to phase-idg-01's scope naming the exact event sequence for the discarded->resolved reversal, and state whether it is a general exception or a revisited+status pair.

findings.subject: phase-idg-13
findings.title: The phase's own next_action and acceptance describe a full-corpus scope that session_budget: 1 cannot obviously hold, reproducing the exact failure mode that split it out of phase-idg-01 in the first place.
findings.evidence: backlog.yaml line 9916: 'The sweep is a read of every idea's findings, so budget for reading 300+ annotations rather than for a mechanical pass.' Acceptance line 2 (line 9902-9903): 'The seven ideas named in scope are closed or explicitly deferred with a reason; a silent omission is a failure of this phase, not a smaller result' — i.e. the acceptance demands a complete sweep of the corpus (432 ideas per my own fold of _data/ideas.jsonl), not just the seven named. GOV-003 line 615-616 gives the reason phase-idg-13 was split out at all: 'the phase's scope had roughly doubled while its session_budget stayed at one.'
findings.consequence: A single-session builder reading 300+ annotations across 400+ ideas and writing individually pointer-verified closes for an unbounded 'rest' risks the same overrun that triggered this phase's own creation, most likely producing an incomplete sweep that acceptance line 2 then calls a failure rather than a partial result.
findings.minimal_fix: Bound the sweep explicitly (e.g. a named batch or a idea-count/date cutoff) rather than 'the rest', or split the backfill into dated batches.
